answer: To prevent malicious swarms from overwhelming the network like an unpredictable zephyr, every autonomous agent must permanently burn an unrecoverable computational thread just to register its presence. Whether a massive algorithmic cartel or a solitary digital sparrow, each node must sink genuine, non-transferable energy into its unique identity credential. By tying validation to un-recyclable expenditure, the economic cost of spawning thousands of fake entities rapidly eclipses any profit an attacker might harvest from manipulating the system.
